documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 04/01/2023
Patient: Maricel Srisai, 28 F
Allergies: NKDA

CC: shortness of breath and racing heart

HPI: 28 year old woman with alpha thalassemia trait, otherwise healthy, two days of breathlessness that has been getting worse, now cannot lie flat and has been sleeping propped on pillows, with a fluttering, fast heartbeat on and off. No chest pain, no fever, no leg swelling, no recent travel. Not pregnant per patient, urine hCG negative.

PMH: alpha-thal trait. Prior SVD. Meds: prenatal vitamin, folic acid 1 mg. SH: never smoker, no EtOH, kindergarten teacher. FH: mother with rheumatic heart disease.

Exam: in mild respiratory distress, speaking full sentences. BP 110/70, HR 120 and irregularly irregular, RR 22, SpO2 94% RA, afebrile. Cardiac: irregular rhythm; low-pitched rumbling diastolic murmur loudest at the apex with an opening snap. Lungs: crackles at both bases. JVP difficult to assess. Extremities without edema.

ECG: atrial fibrillation, rate ~120, no ST or T changes.
CXR: venous congestion, enlarged LA.
Labs: hs troponin 3, BMP normal, CBC with microcytosis consistent with known trait.

ED course: metoprolol 5 mg IV x2 with rate improvement, furosemide 20 mg IV with good urine output and easier breathing. Spontaneously converted to sinus rhythm at about 21:30. Ambulated on room air, SpO2 97%.

Impression: new atrial fibrillation with rapid rate and pulmonary congestion; exam and film most consistent with rheumatic mitral stenosis, given family history.

Disposition: discharged home in sinus rhythm 23:40. Metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily. Furosemide 20 mg daily for 5 days. Needs echocardiogram and cardiology; follow up with PCP within one week. Return for chest pain, worsening breathing or recurrent palpitations.

[Received by fax 4/19/2023 after records request.]

documents.title: Was in the ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello doctor, I went to the emergency room yesterday because I couldn't breathe lying down and my heart was racing. They said my heart was out of rhythm and that I may have a problem with a heart valve, like my mom. They gave me two new pills, metoprolol and a water pill for 5 days. I feel much better today. They told me to see you this week and to get a heart ultrasound. What should I do?

documents.title: RE: Was in the ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you are feeling better. Keep taking both pills as they told you. The office will call tomorrow to get you in this week, I have Thursday morning open. If the racing or breathlessness comes back before then, go back to the ER.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 72. PR, QRS and QT intervals normal. Normal axis. No ST-segment or T-wave abnormality.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: suspected rheumatic mitral stenosis, atrial fibrillation; needs echo

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Seen in ED Sat 4/1 for 2 days of orthopnea, dyspnea and palpitations; per pt and discharge paperwork she was in AF with RVR, CXR with congestion, converted in the ED. Sent home on metoprolol succinate 25 daily and 5 days of furosemide, which she finished yesterday. Since then breathing back to normal, sleeping flat, no palpitations. Mild fatigue first two days on metoprolol, better now. ED told her they suspect a mitral valve problem like her mother's. We do not have the ED record yet, front desk requesting.

O: vitals as charted, regular pulse. Appears well. JVP not elevated. Heart regular, soft low-pitched diastolic rumble at the apex in left lateral position, which I did not hear at her last physical. Lungs clear. No edema.
ECG in office: sinus rhythm 72, normal intervals.

A/P
1. Paroxysmal AF, single episode, now sinus on metoprolol. Check TSH, BMP after diuretic.
2. Probable rheumatic mitral stenosis given exam and her mother's history. Needs TTE and cardiology; referral placed today, asked for a visit within a month.
3. Continue metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily.
Return precautions reviewed. Will call with labs.

documents.title: Thyroid and chemistry results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: TSH normal, so thyroid is not the trigger. Potassium and kidney function fine after the water pill. Cardiology should be calling you to schedule. Let me know if you have not heard from them by next week.

documents.body: Called the hospital ED HIM department, record from 4/1 not sent yet. Faxed a second request with the signed release. They said 5 to 7 business days.

events.reason: suspected rheumatic mitral stenosis, atrial fibrillation

reports.text: Technically adequate study. Left ventricle normal in size and wall thickness with normal systolic function, LVEF 60%. No regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Mitral valve: rheumatic morphology with commissural fusion and diastolic doming of the anterior leaflet. Mitral valve area 1.6 cm2 by planimetry. Mean transmitral gradient 6 mmHg at heart rate 68. Mild mitral regurgitation. Left atrium enlarged, volume index 46 mL/m2. No left atrial thrombus seen on transthoracic imaging. Aortic valve trileaflet, opens normally, no aortic regurgitation. Tricuspid valve normal with trace regurgitation; estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure 36 mmHg. Inferior vena cava normal in size with normal collapse. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Rheumatic mitral stenosis, MVA 1.6 cm2, mean gradient 6 mmHg; mild MR; enlarged left atrium; normal LV function; PASP 36 mmHg.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outpatient Cardiology Consultation
Date of visit: 05/18/2023
Referred by: primary care, for mitral stenosis and atrial fibrillation

Thank you for asking us to see Ms. Srisai, a 28 year old kindergarten teacher with alpha-thalassemia trait, seen in the emergency department on 4/1 with AF and rapid rates and pulmonary congestion that settled with rate control and diuresis, converting to sinus rhythm. She has felt well since, with no palpitations, orthopnea or exertional limitation. She takes metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily, a prenatal vitamin and folic acid. No known drug allergies. Her mother has rheumatic heart disease. She recalls no childhood rheumatic fever. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: BP and HR as recorded, regular rhythm. Loud S1, opening snap, and a low-pitched mid-diastolic rumble at the apex. Lungs clear. No edema.

Echo today: rheumatic mitral valve, MVA 1.6 cm2 by planimetry, mean gradient 6 mmHg at HR 68, mild MR, LA volume index 46 mL/m2, LVEF 60%, PASP 36 mmHg.

Assessment: progressive (stage B) rheumatic mitral stenosis. Her decompensation occurred with AF and fast rates, which shorten diastolic filling. Currently in sinus rhythm.

Recommendations:
1. Continue metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily.
2. Repeat echocardiogram yearly, sooner with symptoms.
3. She mentions she may want a second child. Please have her see us before trying to conceive; pregnancy increases the gradient and needs close follow-up.
4. Seek care promptly for palpitations or breathlessness.
We will see her in 1 year with an echo.

Outside cardiology group
